why: The autonomous run needs a checkable exit condition before implementation

evidence: Sail support matrix and live resp_01a007d1-dfc5-77b0-a79b-02cb9e7b50ad

decision: Used Browserbase Search and Fetch as worker tools
why: Both endpoints passed live credential checks without a browser session
result: Search and Fetch passed

decision: Kept the Grok desktop-chat restraint and reserved visual motion for Fleet activity
why: The reference works through density, spacing, and quiet hierarchy rather than decoration
result: visual direction grounded

decision: Selected a compact journal-first service with SQLite, one run coordinator, SSE replay, and one hot browser store
why: Three candidates converged on the event invariant; the cross-judge preferred candidate 2 but flagged its production package layout as too large for the first complete build
result: VERIFIED design synthesized

decision: Selected UI prototype 1 as the base and kept prototype 2's current-objective block and compact trace footer
why: Prototype 1 kept all agents visible, avoided horizontal overflow, and made the right trace drawer legible at the target viewport
result: VERIFIED in Chrome at 1280 by 768

decision: Scaffolded TanStack Start and upgraded three vulnerable development dependencies before committing
why: The initial audit reported four high or critical advisories; patched Vite, Vitest, and Playwright releases removed them
result: build and audit green

decision: Configured TanStack route generation without blanket lint and type suppressions
why: A fresh comment audit found generator-controlled file-wide suppressions; the router config can remove them without editing generated output
result: three suppressions removed

decision: Separated deterministic, live-worker, and fully live execution profiles in every operator-facing guide
why: A high-throughput product must never blur simulated progress with paid provider output
result: provider and verification boundaries explicit

decision: Removed background execution and request idempotency headers from Sail DeepSeek V4 Flash calls
why: A three-worker live run exposed that Sail's ASAP-only model rejects both request modes; synchronous Responses calls succeed and Fleet still provides durable progress events
result: VERIFIED final run completed with real Sail, Search, and Fetch activity

decision: Added a static interface-copy contract and aligned architecture notes with the implemented route-owned projection
why: The product requirements prohibit eyebrow and uppercase styling, and documentation must describe the shipped state model rather than a proposed abstraction
result: VERIFIED contract runs with the unit suite

decision: Removed automatic Browserbase retries after network exceptions
why: A thrown fetch cannot establish that a paid Search or Fetch request was never accepted, so replay could duplicate cost or side effects
result: VERIFIED one request on ambiguous failure

decision: Applied one HTTP and HTTPS URL schema to Sail tool arguments, Browserbase results, and public Fleet events
why: Generic URL validation accepts file, FTP, and mail schemes that research tools must never fetch
result: VERIFIED unsupported schemes fail before provider calls

decision: Clarified that Sail model turns are synchronous while the coordinator remains outside the HTTP request lifecycle
why: Live verification superseded the earlier shorthand that called Sail workers asynchronous
result: prior grounding retained; runtime boundary corrected

decision: Added a sanitized, reproducible record for the three-worker live-provider run
why: Raw provider responses and ignored SQLite state are not suitable repository evidence
result: live result and Gateway verification gap recorded

decision: Extended the shared web URL boundary to reject literal loopback, private-network, link-local, and IPv6 targets
why: HTTP and HTTPS scheme checks alone still admit non-public destinations
result: local targets fail before provider calls

decision: Normalized trailing DNS dots before public-host checks
why: Fully qualified localhost with a trailing dot resolves to loopback but bypasses an exact hostname comparison
result: localhost and localhost-dot fail before provider calls

decision: Added resolved-address validation and disabled Browserbase redirects
why: Lexical hostname checks cannot detect metadata aliases, private DNS answers, or public-to-private redirects
result: all resolved addresses must be public before one non-redirecting Fetch call

decision: Repeated the live-worker path after DNS enforcement
why: Security controls must preserve the intended Sail plus Browserbase workflow
result: VERIFIED one worker, one Search, three Fetch calls, and synthesis completed

decision: Replaced hand-written IP range checks with ipaddr.js range classification
why: IPv4-mapped IPv6 has multiple canonical forms and denylist parsing missed hexadecimal private addresses
result: mapped loopback, private, and link-local forms classify as non-public

decision: Removed the conversation sidebar and let the chat occupy the full application shell
why: The single-purpose Fleet experience does not need fake navigation or placeholder threads
result: sidebar absent at every viewport

decision: Selected Motion for state-driven inline SVG robots
why: Rive requires a canonical authored asset and dotLottie favors playback; Motion maps agent state directly to character parts and reduced-motion behavior
result: active robots use library-driven rig, eye, arm, antenna, and core motion

decision: Enforced a three-call worker research budget by removing tools from the next Sail turn
why: Actual Chrome runs showed DeepSeek ignoring stop instructions and exhausting all eight turns despite collecting 29 sources
result: workers must synthesize collected evidence instead of looping on Search

decision: Migrated the repository from npm to pnpm 10.22.0
why: One pinned package manager and one lockfile make local installs and browser-test startup reproducible
result: frozen online and offline installs plus every pnpm verification gate passed

decision: Kept orchestration in the conversation and made fleet inspection explicitly user-opened
why: Agent breadth should be visible as progress without forcing users into implementation detail or dumping every finding into the answer
result: Browser flow showed orchestrator progress, no automatic dialog, manual trace inspection, and one synthesized paragraph

decision: Removed the local Playwright suite and standardized visible verification on the Browser plugin
why: The requested verification surface is the actual local application in the in-app browser, while Vitest continues to cover service invariants
result: Browser flow covered both Enter submissions, agent inspection, trace expansion, modal behavior, and final synthesis

decision: Added structured server logs for the complete fleet lifecycle
why: Operators need to see parallel agent, tool, synthesis, timing, and failure progress directly in pnpm dev without exposing credentials or fetched bodies
result: three-agent smoke run produced ordered readable lifecycle logs through completion

decision: Removed execution-profile selection and made every interface launch a full live fleet
why: Development and worker-only modes are implementation and test concerns, not product choices
result: Browser showed one fleet-size dropdown and no execution-profile control

decision: Carried source URLs and agent identities through synthesis into safe linked Markdown
why: A research answer should expose both external evidence and the exact internal trace behind each claim without reconstructing provenance after generation
result: live one-agent Browser run rendered 731 words, 26 source links, 14 agent citations, and opened the cited Frame scout trace

decision: Made individual tool failures recoverable evidence events
why: One source returning 403 must not discard useful Search evidence or fail an entire research angle
result: failed Fetch stayed in trace while the live agent continued to a successful cited synthesis

decision: Aligned the conversation and follow-up composer to one responsive content column
why: Long questions and full-width inputs overwhelmed the research answer on large screens and caused inconsistent gutters across breakpoints
result: Browser measurements at 1280, 820, and 390 pixels showed exact column alignment and zero horizontal overflow

decision: Removed the decorative fleet mark from the welcome-stage center
why: The repeated mark added visual noise above the primary research heading while the persistent header already carries the product identity
result: Browser desktop and 390-pixel mobile renders showed no center mark, retained header branding, and zero horizontal overflow
